label: History
value: Billina was raised in the United States.
unit: Billina was raised in the United States, where her name was originally Bill until Dorothy Gale began calling her Billina. While trapped in a chicken house in the Land of Ev, she fought and defeated a speckled rooster who tried to lord it over her. After Dorothy unlatched the chicken house door and liberated her, Billina was introduced to Dorothy's companions, including the Cowardly Lion and the Hungry Tiger. She accompanied the group into the underground palace of the Nome King, knowing his secret regarding transformations. She surveyed the palace, identified the transformed purple ornaments, and systematically broke the Nome King's enchantments by speaking the word "Ev", restoring the Queen of Ev and her nine children. During her search, she pounced on a small green grasshopper that turned out to be the transformed Princess Ozma; finding it hard and lifeless, she dropped it before swallowing it. After her adventures, she chose to live in the Land of Oz, growing fat and sleek while wearing pearl necklaces and emerald bracelets given to her, residing comfortably in Ozma's palace where she welcomed Dorothy upon her return.

label: History
value: The braided man worked as an inventor.
unit: While living on the surface of the earth, the braided man worked as an inventor and manufacturer of holes for Swiss cheese, porous plasters, doughnuts, and buttons. He eventually invented an adjustable post-hole and joined many together to store them, creating a deep pit. Leaning over to see the bottom, he lost his balance and fell through to a subterranean cavern on Pyramid Mountain. He caught a projecting point of rock to avoid falling into the fiery black waves below and established a home inside a cave. There, he set up a factory producing boxed Assorted Flutters for flags and Rustles for ladies' silk gowns. When Dorothy Gale and her travelers encountered him halfway up Pyramid Mountain, he invited them into his shop and offered his wares. Dorothy presented him with a blue hair-ribbon to complete his collection of hair ties, making him exceedingly happy. In return, he insisted on gifting her a box of rustles and giving the Wizard a box of flutters before bidding them good day.

label: History
value: The Lion encountered Dorothy Gale while traveling through a gloomy forest.
unit: While traveling through a gloomy forest, the Lion encountered Dorothy Gale, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and Toto. After admitting his deep distress over his lack of courage, he accepted Dorothy's invitation to join their journey to the Emerald City to ask the Great Oz for courage. On the way, he fell asleep in a deadly poppy field and had to be rescued on a wooden truck built by the Tin Woodman and pulled by field mice. Upon reaching the Great Oz, he was given a potion from a square green bottle to drink, which made him feel full of courage. Later, during their travels in the West, he was imprisoned by the Wicked Witch until Dorothy melted her and unlocked his cage. In the Emerald City, he welcomed Dorothy back and was introduced to new friends like Jim the cab-horse.

label: History
value: Dorothy lived in a small house
unit: Dorothy lived in a small house on the flat gray prairies of Kansas with her Uncle Henry and Aunt Em. When a severe cyclone struck their farm, Dorothy was unable to reach the storm cellar in time because she stopped to catch her dog, Toto. The cyclone lifted the house high into the air with Dorothy and Toto inside, carrying it far away to the Land of Oz. After arriving in Oz, she embarked on a journey along the yellow brick road to the Emerald City to seek the Wizard's help in returning home, gathering companions including the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion along the way. Sent by the Wizard to defeat the Wicked Witch of the West, Dorothy was captured by the Witch; however, when the Witch stole one of her silver shoes, an angry Dorothy threw a bucket of water over her, unexpectedly causing the Witch to melt away. Dorothy subsequently freed her companions and returned to the Emerald City before finding her way back to Kansas with the assistance of Glinda the Good.

The cyclone lifted the house high into the air with Dorothy and Toto inside, carrying it far away to the Land of Oz. After arriving in Oz, she embarked on a journey along the yellow brick road to the Emerald City to seek the Wizard's help in returning home, gathering companions including the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion along the way. Sent by the Wizard to defeat the Wicked Witch of the West, Dorothy was captured by the Witch; however, when the Witch stole one of her silver shoes, an angry Dorothy threw a bucket of water over her, unexpectedly causing the Witch to melt away. Dorothy subsequently freed her companions and returned to the Emerald City before finding her way back to Kansas with the assistance of Glinda the Good.

label: History
value: Eureka accompanied Dorothy Gale during their subterranean journeys.
unit: Eureka accompanied Dorothy Gale, Zeb, Jim the cab-horse, and the Wizard during their subterranean journeys following a sudden earthquake. When her party was captured and imprisoned in the wooden city of the Gargoyles, Eureka carelessly wandered off by climbing down the outer walls of their prison to observe the inhabitants removing their wings to rest. Later, as the group traversed a dark cavern, Eureka used her keen night vision to identify dangerous dragonettes trapped in rock pockets, warning her companions of the threat. Upon safely reaching the Land of Oz, Eureka was accused of eating Princess Ozma's pet piglet and placed on trial for murder in the throne room. Despite a defense by the Tin Woodman and a staged attempt by him and the Wizard to substitute another piglet, Eureka refused to accept freedom under false pretenses and exposed the deception, ultimately offering to explain the true fate of the missing piglet.

label: History
value: Evardo was sold to the Nome King.
unit: Along with his mother and nine siblings, Evardo was sold to the Nome King by his father, King Evoldo, and transformed into a purple ornament within the underground palace. When Billina the yellow hen discovered the secret to breaking the Nome King's enchantments, she restored Evardo to his true human form alongside the rest of the royal family of Ev. Following their rescue and return to the royal palace in Ev, his mother presented him to the gathered subjects on a balcony as their future ruler. At fifteen years of age, he was crowned King Evardo Fifteenth, being the fifteenth ruler named Evardo in the history of Ev. After receiving the approval of his subjects—including the Wheelers—he bowed to the crowd and went to check the royal pantry for cake.

label: History
value: Evring was born a Prince of Ev.
unit: Evring was born a Prince of Ev, the youngest son of the King and Queen of Ev. His father sold Evring, his mother, and his eight siblings to the Nome King, who transformed Evring into an ornamental purple kitten kept on a mantel in his palace. While exploring the palace to rescue the royal family, Dorothy Gale touched the purple kitten ornament and uttered the word 'Ev', breaking the enchantment and restoring Evring to his human form. Unaware of his period as an ornament, Evring introduced himself to Dorothy and gladly accompanied her through the palace while she attempted to save the rest of his family. He eventually exited the Nome King's palace with Dorothy and was reunited with his mother and siblings after Billina restored them.

label: History
value: General Jinjur's Army of Revolt usurped the throne of the Emerald City.
unit: When General Jinjur's Army of Revolt usurped the throne of the Emerald City, Glinda marched her grand army of girl soldiers to restore order. She pitched her white silk tent outside the city gates and demanded that Jinjur deliver up the wicked witch Mombi as a prisoner. When Jinjur attempted to pass off Jellia Jamb as Mombi using an enchantment, Glinda quickly recognized the deception and restored Jellia to her true form. Glinda then allowed a search within the city, but Mombi disguised herself as a red rose in the palace garden and fled in the form of a Griffin. Glinda gave chase across the country on the untiring Saw-Horse, capturing Mombi on the desert sands by casting a golden thread over her head to neutralize her magic.

value: Glinda returned Mombi to camp in the Gump.

unit: After returning Mombi to camp in the Gump, Glinda interrogated her using a magic white pearl that turned black whenever a lie was spoken. She forced Mombi to confess that the former Wizard of Oz had brought her the infant Princess Ozma, whom Mombi had transformed into the boy Tip. Refusing to perform transformations herself on moral grounds, Glinda made Mombi execute the magical incantation to restore Tip to her true form as Princess Ozma. Glinda then led an airborne assault over the city walls using the Gump, successfully capturing Jinjur and establishing Ozma as the rightful ruler of the Emerald City. Following the victory, Glinda continued to provide wise advice to the young monarch.

label: Personality
value: The Hungry Tiger is a naturally fierce beast.
unit: Despite being a naturally fierce and savage beast, the Hungry Tiger possesses an active conscience that restrains him from acting on his violent desires. He suffers from a constant, insatiable appetite and yearns to devour fat babies or fat little living creatures, yet refuses to commit cruel deeds because he considers it wrong. Although he considers himself a disgracefully bad tiger for acting contrary to his ferocious nature, others regard him as a very good beast. He is polite, humorous, and friendly toward Dorothy and her companions.

label: History
value: The Hungry Tiger was born with a craving for living creatures.
unit: Born with a wild beast's craving for living creatures such as fat babies, the Hungry Tiger chose never to indulge his appetite because his conscience forbade him from performing cruel deeds. Unable to fit in with other wild tigers due to his moral restraint, he abandoned his forest life and united with the Cowardly Lion. Together with the Cowardly Lion, he was hitched to the royal chariot in the Land of Oz. When Dorothy Gale returned to Oz, he met her outside the drawing room of the palace and humorously explained his moral dilemma and perpetual hunger, prompting Dorothy to consider him a good tiger. He later went to the Emerald City with the Cowardly Lion to welcome Dorothy and met Jim the Cab-Horse, engaging in lighthearted banter with the old horse before Dorothy arrived to greet him with affection.

label: History
value: Jack Pumpkinhead was created in Gillikin Country.
unit: Jack Pumpkinhead was created in Gillikin Country by the boy Tip to frighten Mombi, and was brought to life using the Powder of Life. After escaping alongside Tip, Jack accompanied him on a journey toward the Emerald City. During their travels, he assisted Tip with animating the Saw-Horse by holding the creature while Tip attached its bark ears. Upon arriving at the Emerald City, Jack met His Majesty the Scarecrow; despite an initial language misunderstanding, the two bound over their unusual physical natures and became friends, playing a game of quoits together in the palace courtyard. Jack subsequently traveled as part of the Scarecrow's group during their efforts to escape and navigate perils across Oz.

label: History
value: Jim worked as a cab-horse.
unit: Jim worked as a cab-horse before being carried into subterranean realms during an earthquake alongside Zeb and Dorothy Gale. He pulled their buggy through various underground lands, eventually arriving in the Land of Oz. In the Emerald City palace, Jim was provided with a majestic marble room where servants tended to his grooming. Dissatisfied with being offered cooked soup, fish, or roasted quail, he demanded uncooked oatmeal, which the Royal Steward had prepared for him in a tub. The next morning, Jim went out to find grass and encountered the Sawhorse, with whom he debated the nature and merits of a real horse versus a wooden imitation. Upon the arrival of the Cowardly Lion and the Hungry Tiger, Jim was initially terrified, but after being introduced, he bowed with dignity, exchanged banter regarding his conscience, and settled down to eat clover.

unit: Jim worked as a cab-horse before being carried into subterranean realms during an earthquake alongside Zeb and Dorothy Gale. He pulled their buggy through various underground lands, eventually arriving in the Land of Oz. In the Emerald City palace, Jim was provided with a majestic marble room where servants tended to his grooming. Dissatisfied with being offered cooked soup, fish, or roasted quail, he demanded uncooked oatmeal, which the Royal Steward had prepared for him in a tub. The next morning, Jim went out to find grass and encountered the Sawhorse, with whom he debated the nature and merits of a real horse versus a wooden imitation. Upon the arrival of the Cowardly Lion and the Hungry Tiger, Jim was initially terrified, but after being introduced, he bowed with dignity, exchanged banter regarding his conscience, and settled down to eat clover.

label: Personality
value: Jinjur possesses an air of decision.
unit: Jinjur possesses an air of decision, importance, and sharp ambition. She is proud of her army of girls and confident in her cleverness, often scorning male authority and conventional defenses. Despite her cruel threats to dismantle or destroy her non-human opponents, she harbors a deep terror of mice. When deposed, she shows a dramatic flair for despair, moaning at the thought of returning to ordinary domestic work.

label: History
value: Jinjur secretly organized the Army of Revolt.
unit: Jinjur secretly organized the Army of Revolt, assembling girls from all four corners of the Land of Oz to march on the Emerald City and overthrow the Scarecrow. Meeting the boy Tip on the road, she shared her lunch and explained her plan to conquer the city to secure its wealth and gems for her followers. Her army successfully took control of the Emerald City, usurping the throne and installing Jinjur as Queen. When the Scarecrow and his companions confronted her in the throne room, Jinjur had them disarmed and threatened to destroy them all, proposing to turn Jack Pumpkinhead into tarts, the Scarecrow into a bonfire, Nick Chopper into feed for goats, and the Woggle-Bug into soup or goulash. However, the Scarecrow released tiny grey mice from his straw chest, causing Jinjur to jump onto the throne in panic before fleeing the palace alongside her army. She later held out in the palace while surrounded by Glinda's forces, relaxing in a hammock and eating green chocolates until Glinda's party arrived overhead in the Gump. Jinjur was captured, put in chains, and forced to yield the throne. After her army was disbanded and all stolen emeralds were returned, Jinjur was released on a promise of good behavior.

Jinjur was captured, put in chains, and forced to yield the throne. After her army was disbanded and all stolen emeralds were returned, Jinjur was released on a promise of good behavior.

label: History
value: Princess Langwidere is the niece of King Evoldo
unit: As the niece of the late King Evoldo, Princess Langwidere took up residence in a wing of the royal palace in Ev following the royal family's imprisonment by the Nome King. She spent her days spending money from the royal treasury and admiring her thirty interchangeable heads in her mirrored sitting-room. When Dorothy Gale, Tiktok, and Billina arrived at the palace, Langwidere switched her current head (No. 9) to Head No. 17 in her velvet-lined cabinet before granting them an audience. Upon meeting Dorothy, the fiery temperament of Head No. 17 caused her to demand Dorothy's head in exchange for one of her own, and when Dorothy refused, she had the girl imprisoned in a high tower. Later, Princess Ozma arrived with her forces to liberate Dorothy and rescue the royal family of Ev. Ozma confronted Langwidere, leading to Dorothy's release. After the royal family of Ev was saved from the Nome King, the Queen of Ev relieved Langwidere of her administrative duties while permitting her to keep her private rooms and cabinet of heads.

label: History
value: Mombi lived in the Country of the Gillikins.
unit: Mombi lived in the Country of the Gillikins, where she was suspected of practicing magical arts and raised the youth named Tip. In the past, the Wizard of Oz visited her three times to entrust her with the baby Princess Ozma, whom Mombi enchanted and transformed into a boy. When enraged, his face distorts with terrifying anger.

label: History
value: The Nome King rules over a vast subterranean kingdom.
unit: The Nome King rules over a vast subterranean kingdom populated by thousands of rock-fairies and an army of mail-clad Nomes. Having enchanted the Queen of Ev and her ten children, he transformed them into decorative ornaments in his underground palace. When Princess Ozma, Dorothy Gale, and their companions arrived to rescue the royal family, he offered a game in which guests could try to identify the transformed family members, with the catch that failure resulted in the guessers becoming ornaments themselves. After Ozma, the Tin Woodman, and all 26 officers failed and were transformed, the Nome King retreated to his throne room to await further attempts. Later, his face distorted in rage, he mobilized his massive steel-clad army to confront his remaining visitors in his domed cavern.

label: History
value: Ozma is the rightful monarch of the Land of Oz.
unit: Ozma is the rightful monarch of the Land of Oz, descendant of King Oz who originally ruled the united nation before four Witches deposed him. While still an infant, she was stolen by the Wicked Witch Mombi and magically transformed into a boy to prevent her from ever claiming her birthright. Eventually, she escaped from Mombi's power and reclaimed her true identity as Princess Ozma. When General Jinjur briefly took control of the Emerald City from the Scarecrow, Ozma conquered Jinjur with the help of Glinda the Good and took her place as the undisputed Ruler of Oz. Later, Ozma undertook a mission alongside Dorothy Gale to the realm of the Nomes, successfully standing by her companions to rescue the royal family of Ev and search for the missing Tin Woodman. Upon returning to the Emerald City, she hosted Dorothy, Zeb, and the Wizard, generously granting the former humbug Wizard a permanent home as the kingdom's Official Wizard.

Eventually, she escaped from Mombi's power and reclaimed her true identity as Princess Ozma. When General Jinjur briefly took control of the Emerald City from the Scarecrow, Ozma conquered Jinjur with the help of Glinda the Good and took her place as the undisputed Ruler of Oz. Later, Ozma undertook a mission alongside Dorothy Gale to the realm of the Nomes, successfully standing by her companions to rescue the royal family of Ev and search for the missing Tin Woodman. Upon returning to the Emerald City, she hosted Dorothy, Zeb, and the Wizard, generously granting the former humbug Wizard a permanent home as the kingdom's Official Wizard.

label: Appearance
value: The Saw-Horse is a wooden quadruped.
unit: The Saw-Horse is a wooden quadruped constructed out of a log for a body and four stiff legs without knee-joints. Its head originally lacked ears and a neck to turn, but ears made from tree bark were fashioned and inserted into bored holes, alongside a post pounded into its back to serve as a handhold. To prevent its wooden legs from wearing out, Princess Ozma had them shod with plates of gold.

label: History
value: The creature is constructed from a wooden saw-horse.
unit: Constructed from a wooden saw-horse, the creature is brought to life by the boy Tip using Mombi's Powder of Life. Upon awakening, it initially prances in circles due to having no neck to turn and lacks ears to hear commands until Tip whittles bark ears for it. Tip also hammers a riding post into its back so Jack Pumpkinhead can ride without wearing out his wooden joints. The Saw-Horse serves as the primary mount for the party's journey to the Emerald City and aids in their escape from the rebel forces. During their travels, its long new leg requires the Tin Woodman to chop it down so the horse can walk comfortably. It later participates in various exploits across Oz and surrounding lands, including fighting off enemies with its legs and serving as Princess Ozma's royal steed.

unit: Constructed from a wooden saw-horse, the creature is brought to life by the boy Tip using Mombi's Powder of Life. Upon awakening, it initially prances in circles due to having no neck to turn and lacks ears to hear commands until Tip whittles bark ears for it. Tip also hammers a riding post into its back so Jack Pumpkinhead can ride without wearing out his wooden joints. The Saw-Horse serves as the primary mount for the party's journey to the Emerald City and aids in their escape from the rebel forces. During their travels, its long new leg requires the Tin Woodman to chop it down so the horse can walk comfortably. It later participates in various exploits across Oz and surrounding lands, including fighting off enemies with its legs and serving as Princess Ozma's royal steed.

label: Appearance
value: The Scarecrow is made from a suit of faded blue clothes.
unit: The Scarecrow is made from a suit of faded blue clothes stuffed unevenly with straw, giving his arms and legs a bumpy, flimsy, and awkward look. His head consists of a small straw-stuffed sack with eyes, ears, a nose, and a mouth rudely painted on it. Padded cotton gloves form his hands, and wisps of straw protrude from his coat, neck, and boot-tops. While serving as king, he wears a heavy golden crown thick with sparkling jewels that causes his painted brow to sag in wrinkles.

label: Personality
value: The Scarecrow is widely regarded as the wisest personage in the Land of Oz.
unit: Widely regarded as the wisest personage in the Land of Oz, the Scarecrow is thoughtful, considerate, and polite. He maintains a gay, charming, and optimistic demeanor, remaining cheerful even in the face of danger. He cares deeply for his companions, showing particular empathy and consideration for those made of flesh and blood who tire or hunger. Though sometimes given to mild teasing or dry humor, he possesses a strong sense of justice and modesty regarding his royal standing.

label: History
value: The Scarecrow was originally created in a cornfield.
unit: The Scarecrow was originally created in a cornfield and later joined Dorothy Gale on her quest to the Emerald City to ask the Wizard for a brain. After the Wizard granted his request and subsequently departed, the Scarecrow was made the ruler of the Emerald City. During his reign, he received Jack Pumpkinhead and engaged Jellia Jamb as an interpreter before realizing that all inhabitants of Oz spoke the same language. Shortly thereafter, Queen Jinjur led an Army of Revolt that deposed him, forcing him and his companions—including Tip, Jack, the Woggle-Bug, and the Tin Woodman—to flee and plot an escape from captivity. He later reunited with Dorothy and joined various adventures, including campaigns in the Land of Ev and assisting Princess Ozma in governance and trials within the Emerald City.

value: Gwig is the Sorcerer of the Mangaboos.
unit: Gwig, the Sorcerer of the Mangaboos, encountered the Wizard when the latter arrived in the glass city. He corrected the Wizard for mispronouncing the name Mangaboos and challenged him to prove his sorcery skills before the Prince. Gwig performed his usual sorcery demonstration by waving his thorny hand to make invisible tinkling bells produce sweet music throughout the glass hall. After examining the Wizard's empty hat, he watched the Wizard create and manipulate nine tiny piglets, ultimately being acknowledged by the Prince as inferior to the Wizard in magical power.

label: History
value: Tiktok was manufactured by the firm Smith & Tinker.
unit: Tiktok was manufactured by the firm Smith & Tinker in Evna as an automatic mechanical clockwork person equipped with separate mechanisms for thought, speech, and action. After being purchased by King Ev-oldo of the Land of Ev, he was eventually locked inside a concealed rock cavern atop a seaside mound. Dorothy Gale discovered the secret chamber and used a golden key to unlock the stone door, where she found the idle copper man. After being wound up, Tiktok pledged his service to Dorothy and accompanied her and Billina through the Land of Ev. Along the way, he defended them from the mischievous Wheelers by capturing their leader and forcing him to clear a path. He guided Dorothy to Princess Langwidere's palace, where he helped secure an audience. Later, he joined Princess Ozma's expeditionary force to the Nome King's underground realm to rescue the captive Queen of Ev and her children. During diplomatic negotiations, Tiktok advised Ozma on how to address the Nome King politely and assured the party of the monarch's underlying honesty.

label: History
value: The Tin Woodman traveled to the Emerald City.
unit: The Tin Woodman traveled to the Emerald City alongside Dorothy, the Scarecrow, and the Cowardly Lion to seek a heart from the Great Oz. After returning from defeating the Wicked Witch, he threatened Oz with his axe when the Wizard delayed keeping his promises, leading to the discovery that Oz was merely a common man and a humbug. During Queen Jinjur's siege of the Emerald City palace, he remained trapped inside with the Scarecrow, Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Woggle-Bug, polishing his tin chest while discussing escape plans and opposing any ideas of eating Jack or the Woggle-Bug. When Glinda captured old Mombi, the Tin Woodman suggested trying to conquer the witch with kindness and expressed relief upon learning Glinda's death threat was only a bluff. Later, during the trial of Eureka the kitten, he agreed to assist the Wizard in hiding a duplicate piglet inside his funnel-shaped hat to trick the court and save the kitten's life.

label: History
value: Tip grew up on a farm.
unit: Tip grew up on a farm where he made a wooden dummy with a carved pumpkin head named Jack Pumpkinhead to scare the old witch Mombi. After Mombi animated Jack with the Powder of Life, Tip secretly observed her spellwork. When Tip later set out toward the Emerald City to rejoin Jack Pumpkinhead and the Saw-Horse, he ran out of food and encountered General Jinjur on the roadside. Jinjur shared her lunch with him, and Tip carried her basket while learning about her secret Army of Revolt and their plot to overthrow the Scarecrow. Later, Tip helped construct and bring to life a magical flying creature known as the Gump, commanding it to fly his companions southward toward Glinda the Good. During the aerial flight, Tip discovered three silver pills and a written note inside a false bottom of Mombi's discarded pepper-box.

label: History
value: Uncle Henry lived on a small farm on the Kansas prairies.
unit: Uncle Henry lived and worked on a small farm on the Kansas prairies with his wife, Aunt Em, and his orphan niece, Dorothy. When a sudden cyclone hit their farm, he ran to secure the livestock while Dorothy and her dog were carried away in the house. After Dorothy's eventual return, his health suffered, leading him to travel across the ocean to Australia with Dorothy to rest. He stayed in Sydney while Dorothy visited friends in San Francisco and later paid a visit to Uncle Bill Hugson at Hugson's Ranch in California. Through Ozma's magic picture, Dorothy observed him sitting sad and thin in Sydney, smoking his pipe, which prompted her to use magic to reunite with him.

After Dorothy's eventual return, his health suffered, leading him to travel across the ocean to Australia with Dorothy to rest. He stayed in Sydney while Dorothy visited friends in San Francisco and later paid a visit to Uncle Bill Hugson at Hugson's Ranch in California. Through Ozma's magic picture, Dorothy observed him sitting sad and thin in Sydney, smoking his pipe, which prompted her to use magic to reunite with him.

label: History
value: The Wicked Witch of the West ruled over the Winkies.
unit: The Wicked Witch of the West ruled over the Winkies in the uncultivated Country of the West, keeping the local population in servitude. When Dorothy Gale and her companions traveled into her territory to destroy her, the Witch spotted them from her castle door using her single telescopic eye. She blew her silver whistle to send a pack of forty great wolves to tear them to pieces, but the Tin Woodman slaughtered the entire pack. Next, she summoned a flock of wild crows to peck out their eyes, but they too were slain. She then sent her slaves to attack, but they were frightened away by the Cowardly Lion. Having exhausted her other options, the Witch donned the Golden Cap and invoked its magical charm for the third and final time, summoning the Winged Monkeys. She commanded them to destroy the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, capture the Lion to harness him like a horse, and bring Dorothy to her castle. Because Dorothy bore the kiss of the Good Witch and wore the Silver Shoes, neither the Monkeys nor the Wicked Witch could harm her directly, so the Witch forced Dorothy into kitchen labor while holding the Lion prisoner in a fenced yard. After tricking Dorothy to steal one of her Silver Shoes, Dorothy threw a bucket of water over her in anger, causing the Wicked Witch of the West to melt completely away.

label: History
value: The Wizard formerly ruled the Emerald City for many years.
unit: After formerly ruling the Emerald City for many years and overseeing its construction, the Wizard left the Land of Oz and returned to Omaha. Finding his old friends gone or deceased, he rejoined the circus as a balloonist for Bailum & Barney's Great Consolidated Shows. During a balloon ascension, an earthquake caused him to fall into a deep crack in the earth, descending into the subterranean Land of the Mangaboos. There, he reunited with Dorothy Gale and met the Prince and the local Sorcerer. After traveling through underground realms, including the Valley of Voe, he eventually reached the surface kingdom of Oz once again. Upon his return, Princess Ozma offered him a permanent home as the Official Wizard of her kingdom, which he accepted with emotional gratitude.

label: History
value: The Woggle-Bug escaped the schoolhouse in his magnified form.
unit: After escaping the schoolhouse in his magnified form and acquiring tailored clothes, the Woggle-Bug encountered Tip, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Saw-Horse, joining them on their journey to the Emerald City. He suggested using one of Jack's wooden legs to replace a broken leg on the Saw-Horse. During their aerial journey on the Gump toward Glinda's territory, he frequently made puns that annoyed Tip and the Scarecrow. He was eventually appointed Dean of the Royal College of Athletic Science in Oz. Later, at the palace of Princess Ozma, he was introduced to the Wizard of Oz, where he introduced himself boastfully before sitting in a corner to read.

label: History
value: Zeb was driving Jim in a buggy.
unit: Zeb was driving his horse Jim in a buggy when a sudden earthquake tore open the earth, causing him, Dorothy Gale, Jim, and Dorothy's cat Eureka to fall through a great subterranean abyss. As they floated safely down onto a transparent roof in a glass city inside the hollow earth, Zeb accidentally kicked over Eureka's birdcage while stepping out of the buggy. He courageously tested walking on the solid air to lead Dorothy down to the glass pavement below. When confronted by a local official who accused them of causing damage via a rain of stones, Zeb explained the earthquake had caused it, and the group was directed to the House of the Sorcerer. Throughout their subterranean journey, Zeb cared for Jim by unharnessing him and assisting the Wizard in defending their group against wooden Gargoyles, during which he captured a crowned Gargoyle by binding it with a leather strap. Eventually arriving safely in the Land of Oz, Zeb was amazed by the splendor of the Emerald City palace, where he bathed and dressed in maroon velvet. During a festival day, Zeb competed in games outside the city gates, wrestling with a little Munchkin champion who laid him on his back three times; when Zeb challenged him to a boxing match and boxed his ears, the Munchkin burst into tears, amusing the crowd and Princess Ozma. Zeb then helped set up a race between Jim and the Sawhorse.

As they floated safely down onto a transparent roof in a glass city inside the hollow earth, Zeb accidentally kicked over Eureka's birdcage while stepping out of the buggy. He courageously tested walking on the solid air to lead Dorothy down to the glass pavement below. When confronted by a local official who accused them of causing damage via a rain of stones, Zeb explained the earthquake had caused it, and the group was directed to the House of the Sorcerer. Throughout their subterranean journey, Zeb cared for Jim by unharnessing him and assisting the Wizard in defending their group against wooden Gargoyles, during which he captured a crowned Gargoyle by binding it with a leather strap. Eventually arriving safely in the Land of Oz, Zeb was amazed by the splendor of the Emerald City palace, where he bathed and dressed in maroon velvet. During a festival day, Zeb competed in games outside the city gates, wrestling with a little Munchkin champion who laid him on his back three times; when Zeb challenged him to a boxing match and boxed his ears, the Munchkin burst into tears, amusing the crowd and Princess Ozma. Zeb then helped set up a race between Jim and the Sawhorse.
